problem.title: At Least One Zero
problem.statement: How many three-digit positive integers contain at least one digit equal to 0?
hints: Counting zero in the tens and zero in the ones creates overlap. What is the complete opposite?
Count all three-digit numbers, then count those with no zero.

solutionSteps.title: Count the whole
solutionSteps.body: There are 9 choices for the hundreds digit and 10 choices for each remaining digit, so there are 9 × 10 × 10 = 900 three-digit numbers.

solutionSteps.title: Count the complement
solutionSteps.body: A number with no zero has 9 choices in each position, giving 9 × 9 × 9 = 729 numbers.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract
solutionSteps.body: Every three-digit number either has at least one zero or has no zero. Therefore the desired count is 900 − 729 = 171.

notes: Direct zero-position groups overlap; the no-zero complement is exhaustive and disjoint from the target.

problem.title: Lantern Signals
problem.statement: A signal has four lights in a row. Each light is red, blue, or green. How many color patterns have at least one red light?
hints: What colors can appear in a pattern with no red light?

solutionSteps.title: Count all patterns
solutionSteps.body: Each of the four lights has 3 choices, so there are 3⁴ = 81 patterns.

solutionSteps.title: Count no-red patterns
solutionSteps.body: With no red, every light must be blue or green, giving 2⁴ = 16 patterns.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract
solutionSteps.body: Every pattern has at least one red or has no red, so the desired count is 81 − 16 = 65.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of all 81 four-light patterns

problem.title: At Least One Even Spin
problem.statement: A spinner has four equal sections labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4. It is spun three times, and the ordered sequence of results is recorded. How many result sequences contain at least one even number?
hints: What does a sequence with no even result look like?
Subtract the all-odd sequences from all ordered sequences.

solutionSteps.title: Count every sequence
solutionSteps.body: There are 4 choices on each of three spins, so there are 4³ = 64 ordered sequences.

solutionSteps.title: Count the complement
solutionSteps.body: A sequence with no even result uses only 1 or 3 on each spin, giving 2³ = 8 all-odd sequences.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract
solutionSteps.body: Every sequence is all odd or contains at least one even result, so 64 − 8 = 56 sequences work.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of 64 ordered spin sequences
notes: The complement is all three results odd, not merely one odd result.

problem.title: Repeated Symbol Badge
problem.statement: A three-symbol badge is made from the symbols A, B, C, D, and E. Repetition is allowed, and order matters. How many badges use at least one symbol more than once?
hints: The repeated-symbol badges come in several shapes. What is their complete opposite?
Count badges with three different symbols.

solutionSteps.title: Count all badges
solutionSteps.body: With 5 choices for each of 3 positions, there are 5³ = 125 badges.

solutionSteps.title: Count all-different badges
solutionSteps.body: There are 5 choices for the first symbol, then 4 unused choices, then 3, for 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 badges.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract
solutionSteps.body: Every badge is either all different or has at least one repeated symbol, so 125 − 60 = 65 badges have a repeat.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of all 125 ordered badges
notes: The desired set includes exactly one pair and three equal symbols; the all-distinct complement removes both cases at once.

problem.title: Two Special Officers
problem.statement: A club has six students, including Maya and Noah. One student is chosen as captain and a different student as recorder. How many officer assignments include at least one of Maya or Noah?
hints: How many assignments use neither Maya nor Noah?

solutionSteps.title: Count the whole
solutionSteps.body: There are 6 choices for captain and then 5 different choices for recorder, giving 6 × 5 = 30 assignments.

solutionSteps.title: Count neither student
solutionSteps.body: Using neither Maya nor Noah leaves 4 choices for captain and then 3 for recorder, giving 4 × 3 = 12 assignments.

solutionSteps.title: Subtract
solutionSteps.body: Every remaining assignment includes Maya or Noah in at least one role, so 30 − 12 = 18 assignments work.

validationMethods: exhaustive enumeration of 30 ordered officer assignments
notes: Direct Maya/Noah role cases overlap when both students serve; the neither-student complement avoids that overlap.
